messages:
Anya: Quick report 1: brought up reranker v4-ptq-perlayer on the validation holdout. Overall NDCG@10 +1.4% but MRR@1 -4.5%. Not sure why head drops this much while top-k improves.

Rafael: big MRR@1 drops usually mean top-1 flips. Could be candidate normalization or tie-breaking. Did you run with the same candidate dedupe order?

Anya: yes, candidate pool identical. Sampling seed same. PTQ used per-layer min-max with batch calibration on 1k examples from production-like traffic.

Priya: did the calibration set include short queries? our calibration skews if short queries underrepresented -> scale collapses for those cases.

Anya: calibration distribution: mean query length 18 tokens, but holdout short-query slice median is 6. good catch.

Ben: can you paste the eval run and the quick percentiles for scores?

```# eval
python -m eval.rerank --model models/v4-ptq-perlayer.pt --queries holdout.jsonl \
  --candidates candidates.jsonl --metrics ndcg@10,mrr@1 --seed 2026

# quick stats
jq -r '.scores | map(.score) | add' scores.jsonl # (not real, illustrative)
```

Anya: raw percentiles from float baseline vs ptq-perlayer:
float p1=-0.6 p50=0.14 p99=1.5
ptq p1=-0.08 p50=0.06 p99=0.9
Looks like range contracted again.

Priya: contraction again. For PTQ per-layer we expect some variance loss but not that dramatic. Which layers used symmetric quant? Any clipping settings?

Anya: used symmetric for activations, per-channel for weights; clipping at 99.9 percentile.

Rafael: two experiments: 1) re-calibrate with stratified sample (include short-query heavy slice) 2) try asymmetric activation quant with per-tensor zero-point to preserve negative tails.

Anya: started stratified calibration with 20% short queries. eval-bot kicked off job_351900.

eval-bot: job_351900 started (Anya) 1: stratified-calib, asymmetric-acts, seed=2026.

Ben: also add a tiny post-quant affine on output logits (learned scalar on calibration set) as a quick hack; sometimes it restores head without retraining.

Anya: quick hack results: post-affine alpha=1.6 beta=-0.02 -> MRR@1 recovered to -0.6% vs float, NDCG@10 +1.1%.

Priya: and stratified calibration results?

Anya: stratified-calib + asymmetric activations: MRR@1 -0.2%, NDCG@10 +1.3%. Best so far.

Rafael: so root cause is calibration sampling + symmetric clipping. Short queries create sharp logits that get squashed. Asymmetric quant + better sampling preserves head variance.

Ben: can we get per-query diagnostics for the top-1 flips? a tiny script to list queries where top1 changes and their token counts / candidate counts would help.

Anya: ran per-query diff. Top1 flips concentrated on queries <=8 tokens and candidate sets >30. Sketch:
```
# pseudocode
for q in holdout:
  f_top = topk(float_model, q, k=1)
  q_top = topk(ptq_model, q, k=1)
  if f_top != q_top:
    emit(q.id, len(q.tokens), len(q.candidates))
```
Collected 1.9k flips; 78% are <=8 tokens.

Priya: ok actionable: 1) default onboarding: use stratified calibration that matches target traffic slices (short/long) 2) prefer asymmetric activation quant for reranker arch 3) add post-quant logistic-rescale as fallback with documented params in model card.

Rafael: also add unit test: when we quantize, assert p1/p99 ratios stay within [0.25, 1.25] of float baseline OR flag for manual review.

Ben: created ticket INF-1432 for quant-onboard-checks + example thresholds. Assigning to infra + eval.

Anya: I'll update the PR: include calibration sampling config, set asymmetric acts flag, and add optional post-rescale hook. Will run canary after merge.

eval-bot: job_351900 finished 1: stratified-calib run complete; artifacts at s3://redwood-evals/351900/

Priya: when you publish model-card, include a short note: "Calibration: stratified (short/medium/long), Quant: per-channel weights, asymmetric activations, post-quant rescale alpha=1.6 beta=-0.02 (canary only)"

Anya: will do. Also adding a lightweight regression dashboard that charts p1/p50/p99 and top1-flip-count across releases.

Rafael: nice. That dashboard + INF-1432 should stop repeated surprises.

Anya: thanks everyone. Follow-ups: PR+canary, INF-1432, dashboard spike. Closing for now unless new anomalies show up. :white_check_mark:
